tasks.short: Attend professional meetings, conferences and teacher workshops

steps.what: Attend professional meetings, educational conferences and teacher training workshops and participate in learning

tasks.design: Retain teacher attendance and participation. Session materials in {DOCS} may support learning, but a summary is not counted as replacing workshop practice or discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competence develops through practice, questions and exchange rather than receipt of text alone.
tasks.enabler_now: No technology change is required for this unchanged activity.
tasks.still_hard: Connecting ideas from a session to the teacher's own group.
tasks.human_edge: Ask relevant questions and test an approach with peers.
tasks.altitude: Professional learning time and responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a workshop addresses a teaching need
reach.learn: Professional learning goals and practical evaluation

evidence.claim: Workshop attendance includes learning and peer exchange that is not replaced by automating a summary.

assumptions: Boundary is attendance and participation, not event booking, travel reimbursement or creating training materials.
No structured completion flag or machine action is used; all learning time remains in s1.
Native document access is sufficient; no software build is proposed. Zero incremental upkeep because the workflow and material access are unchanged.
research_questions: Which sessions depend on practical participation or discussion rather than passive reading?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Attendance and professional learning retain all time; replacing them with a summary is not a saving in this design.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare required reports on children and activities

steps.what: Select and verify student observations and activity records for the reporting period
Assemble student and activity data into the required report form
Write descriptive report comments from the verified observations

loop.purpose: Draft concise descriptive comments without inventing child characteristics
loop.input: Teacher-verified dated observations and the populated report sections
loop.output: Draft comments with observation references for every factual statement
loop.check: Teacher compares every comment with original observations, verifies meaning and qualifiers, and removes unsupported or diagnostic claims
loop.stop: One draft per report section; unsupported or unsuitable wording is written manually, with no autonomous revisions or sending
loop.why_not_simpler: Native fields handle the form, but concise prose connecting free-text observations needs language interpretation; use the loop only if reusable wording is insufficient

steps.what: Review reports for accuracy, completeness and privacy before releasing them to administration

tasks.design: Configure a report template from verified records in {LMS} and {DOCS}. If native fields and reusable wording are insufficient, a bounded model drafts descriptive comments from selected observations; the teacher checks their meaning and releases the completed report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations and activity details must be gathered, copied and described without overstating what they show.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report fields can remove copying, with a bounded draft for narrative sections only.
tasks.still_hard: Representing a child fairly from incomplete observations and protecting sensitive details.
tasks.human_edge: Know the context behind an observation and recognise an unfair generalisation.
tasks.altitude: Less report assembly; the teacher retains responsibility for every claim and recipient.

reach.task: Clarify what information a required activity report actually needs
reach.learn: Report purpose, access controls and data minimisation

evidence.claim: ParnasSys provides pupil records, learning-goal tracking and a parent app; this supports a record-system context, not a claim that it generates these narrative reports.
A source-bounded language draft can assist descriptive report writing if a teacher checks every statement; the saving here is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing a required report from existing observations, not observing children, making assessments or conducting parent meetings. No automated grade, developmental diagnosis or support allocation is proposed.

Teacher produces the verified packet in s1: child or group id, reporting period, activity date, observation text, source reference and intended report section. All 30 hours of selection, correction and missing-note capture remain; existing original observation capture is unchanged outside this reporting task.
s2 retains 5 hours for identity, date and field mapping checks; missing or conflicting records trigger manual assembly. s3 retains 15 hours for semantic checking and manual prose fallback.
Test native reports and approved wording first. Only approved processing with minimal necessary child data is allowed; if unavailable, write narrative manually and use the lower scenario.
s4 approves the completed form and comments after they exist; every edit voids approval. Existing storage and model runtime are not labour savings.
research_questions: Can each report sentence be traced to a teacher-verified observation without turning a specific event into a general label?

already_counted.description: Verify source notes, check mappings, review narrative meaning and release the report

incremental.description: Maintain report mappings and audit narrative examples for unsupported claims

approvals.approved_version: Final report revision including all populated fields, narrative and recipient scope; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+5+15+20=70; gross 30 minus upkeep 2 gives net 28. E1 scenario reduces assembly by 80% and narrative writing by 40%, retaining source gathering and final review. Missing notes, unsuitable drafts or unavailable approved processing may absorb the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on developing, evaluating and revising preschool programs

steps.what: Collaborate with teachers and administrators to evaluate preschool programs and discuss changes
Develop and revise preschool program proposals with colleagues

tasks.design: Keep program evaluation and joint revision with teachers and administrators using the existing shared {DOCS} proposal. Do not add an assumed minutes or retyping baseline to a task centred on joint educational decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program choices involve educational priorities and different practical perspectives.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared documents already support joint editing without changing the underlying judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving trade-offs and deciding what a revised program should prioritise.
tasks.human_edge: Bring classroom experience and negotiate a workable shared proposal.
tasks.altitude: Collaboration time and program approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Compare a program revision with curriculum progression
reach.learn: Program evaluation and developmentally appropriate progression

evidence.claim: Joint program evaluation and substantive revision require educational judgement and agreement; existing document editing does not remove that work.

assumptions: Boundary includes only this teacher's contribution; colleagues' time and the program leader's final decision stay outside the denominator.
Teacher produces proposed changes through discussion and editing in the retained steps; no structured preference score or automated program decision is used.
Native shared editing is already available and earns no new saving. Zero incremental upkeep because there is no new tool, feed or meeting-capture process.
research_questions: Is any substantial repeated clerical work present beyond the substantive discussion and revision?

already_counted.description: Discuss educational changes and revise the shared proposal

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net zero. Retain collaboration and substantive revision; no unobserved meeting paperwork is treated as saved time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan experiential activities and supervise children's learning

steps.what: Plan class projects, field trips, guest visits and other experiential activities
Arrange people, materials and permissions for the planned activity
Supervise class projects, field trips and visits and adapt to children's needs
Guide students in reflecting on and learning from the activity

tasks.design: Reuse an activity checklist and invitation fields in {DOCS}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. The teacher confirms arrangements and permissions manually, then retains all supervision and guided reflection with the children.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated coordination messages sit around an activity that must remain supervised.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and shared checklists can reuse the selected plan without generating a safety decision.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected needs, missing permissions and the realities of the venue or guest activity.
tasks.human_edge: Keep children safe while helping them notice and learn from the experience.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated coordination text; supervision time and authority do not change.

reach.task: Prepare an inclusive participation arrangement for an activity
reach.learn: Support needs, supervision responsibilities and contingency planning

evidence.claim: Reusable invitations and activity checklists can reduce coordination entry without replacing teacher planning, permissions checks or physical supervision.

assumptions: Boundary includes teacher planning, coordination, supervision and reflection; family replies, guest preparation and additional adults' unchanged time are outside the denominator.

Teacher produces date, location, activity, intended participants, materials and supervision proposal in s1 with all 20 hours retained. In s2 the teacher captures replies and verifies permissions, recipient list and staffing in its retained 9 hours; no structured consent flag is assumed free or inferred from silence.
Existing administrative contacts are checked manually in s2. Missing replies, unsuitable staffing or incomplete permissions stop the arrangement and use manual follow-up.
Test native templates and checklists before custom workflow. The saving is repeated message preparation only, not supervision or a safety assessment.
s2 confirms the exact arrangement message; later changes require checking again and do not grant automatic trip authorisation.
unknowns: Frequency of trips versus in-class projects
research_questions: How much coordination time is repeated text rather than permissions checking and exception handling?

already_counted.description: Plan the activity, verify arrangements and permissions, supervise and guide reflection

incremental.description: Maintain activity checklist and invitation fields

approvals.approved_version: Final arrangement message with date, location, participants and required permissions; changes void confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+9+45+20=94; gross 6 minus upkeep 1 gives net 5. E1 scenario reduces coordination preparation by 40% only. One-off trips and missing replies may consume all gains; supervision and learning time stay intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher has less report assembly and repeated activity messaging, with professional learning, collaboration and supervision retained.
reach: Coordinate inclusive activity arrangements with assistants
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who can produce traceable reports efficiently and preserve time for children, colleagues and professional learning.
